chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, raising it (mursal), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How far is it between you and the Euphrates?' So I informed him. So he said: 'If I were in its presence, I would love to go to it at the two ends of the day.'

key_terms.الْفُرَات: The Euphrates River (Arabic: al-Furat), a sacred river in Shia tradition
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Technical hadith term indicating a mursal (incomplete) chain; the narrator skips intermediate transmitters to reach the Imam
key_terms.طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ: The two ends of the day — morning and evening; idiom for visiting twice daily

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about visiting the Euphrates River?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses his deep love for the Euphrates River, asking a companion about its distance and declaring that he would visit it morning and evening if he lived nearby. This hadith is part of a chapter dedicated to the virtues and merits of the Euphrates River, a river held sacred in Shia tradition for its significance to the Imams and the tragedy of Karbala. The historical context connects to the fact that Imam Husayn (AS) and his companions reached the banks of the Euphrates before the events of Karbala.
